pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as four days of full-body kettlebells plus mobility, walking and stretching on the other three, with the C5/C6 explicitly folded into the mobility work. The prospect had effectively pre-agreed the shape — 'I'll do four days a week and I'll probably do some walking and some stretching on the other days' — and closed the topic with 'the proof will be in the... Proof's in the pudding'. Understood, agreed, no questions.

This was the only pillar he engaged back on. 'It'd be interesting to see the nutrition stuff as well. It's not as stringent... when you used the word sustainable, that allows you to, because... if you're eating certain things and you're at home every day, it's really easy. And then if you're not at home, that's the time that it becomes more difficult.' He then probed the mechanics — whether quantities are given and whether there is a free day each week — and the rep confirmed both.

Rep delivered 24/7 Trevor access, weekly check-ins, form video review and chasing on missed workouts and nutrition ticks: 'if you don't tick that you've done that workout we're going to be on [you]... we're going to hold you accountable'. The prospect gave no reaction at all, despite having named accountability as his actual gap ('just lacking the discipline'). The one pillar built for his stated problem drew no response — the rep did not tie it back to his own words.

anchors.raw: in the past, you know, like Keith Webber, I've got a bunch of his stuff, you know, where he did the videos, and you sort of get three of the routines off those videos
anchors.note: He already owns a one-off-purchase video library that delivers programming, plus free Instagram sets. His stated deficit is adherence, not content, so the substitute is genuinely functional on the content axis — it just does not do accountability. The rep touched this ('it's a good job that we don't have to teach you everything from scratch') but never priced the difference between owning programmes and being held to them.

anchors.raw: Look, the only thing was the cost that was higher than I was expecting
anchors.note: He arrived with a lower number in his head and said so directly. Nothing in the call had established a value stake before the number landed, so the gap had nothing to close against.

anchors.raw: I just dropped 150 to 170 grand on building materials last week. So we're, there's a lot going out.
anchors.note: Not an affordability anchor — it is a liquidity-timing anchor, and a strong one. He has demonstrably large discretionary capital and explicitly said the fee 'wouldn't be crippling financially', but a house build creates a joint forecast conversation that a personal purchase would not. This is the actual mechanism of the deferral and the rep read it as a spouse objection instead.

anchors.raw: For the six months in Aussie dollars, it's 8.4k to round up. It's like 8,380-something, if I was to convert it roughly off the top of my head.
anchors.note: Quoting a converted local-currency figure the rep computed mentally makes the number look both larger and less authoritative than the standard USD tier. He then repeated it as a precise 8,388 in the reframe, giving a made-up-sounding exactness to an admittedly rough conversion.

unmet_demand.want: Training that is safe to load around cervical spinal stenosis with radicular symptoms — 'if I have compression, they can shoot down my arm'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme's core library is loaded ballistic kettlebell work including snatches, which puts repeated overhead and cervical-loading demand on exactly the segment involved. The rep asserted the mobility pillar would help the C5/C6 get 'all better' and that the first month is form at lighter weight, but nothing in the call established that the programme can be run safely for this condition or that anyone qualified had said so.

unmet_demand.want: A deliberate build-up phase before returning to previous intensity — 'I better build up for a month or so before I start really steaming into it again'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Actually served. The rep answered 'That's what we do anyway' and described the first month as form mastery at lighter weight. Recorded only because it was the prospect's own explicit ask and it was answered in four words rather than used.
